utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. There are a few matters, very limited -- yes, first I should invite Madam Registrar to call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I'd first like to briefly put on the record a matter that remains from yesterday; that is, the line in the statement of the present witness, paragraph 12. We noticed yesterday that, at least for outsiders it was visible, that the words "Konjevic Polje" were missing in the English translation. We asked to start with -- with CLSS to it is whether there was anything more than just that "Konjevic Polje" was mentioned as where the witness was certain that he did not see Momir Nikolic on the 13th of July, and indeed it doesn't say any more. So therefore, although this is not new translation, but we were informed that the English translation of that second sentence of paragraph 12 should read: "What I am completely certain of is that on that day, the 13th of July, in Konjevic Polje I did not see Momir Nikolic, whom I knew very well personally." So that at least that we don't have to guess what role Konjevic Polje plays in the English translation. Then one other matter is about the possible video-conference link testimony for Ratko Skrbic. On the 16th of February, the Chamber invited the Defence to postpone the testimony of Ratko Skrbic until it was in a position to advise the Chamber whether or not it intended to put additional questions to the witness and whether or not there would be a related request for video-conference link testimony. The Chamber notes that Skrbic has since reappeared on the Defence schedule, but the Chamber still has not been informed about these issues. And therefore in the absence of additional information from the Defence, the Chamber understands that there will be no further questions, apart from the attestation, and no cross-examination, and accordingly Skrbic can be added to the existing scheduled video-conference link.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session, briefly.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Perhaps we could deal with one other matter, which is about Exhibit P7019. On the 17th of December of last year, the Prosecution e-mailed the Chamber and the Defence stating that it had received a more legible version of P7019. This version, along with its English translation, has been uploaded into e-court. The Chamber hereby instructs the Registry to replace P7019 with the revised version uploaded under 65 ter number 06444a. Further, the Registry is instructed to inform the Chamber and the parties when the replacement has been made, and for the parties to make any additional submissions within regard to admission within seven days of this date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, I'd like to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony. Mr. Gillett will now continue his cross-examination. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, and Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Blagojevic. Yesterday --

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Yesterday at the end of the day we were speaking about the events at the Vuk Karadzic school in Bratunac on 14 July. Now, that day, Muslim prisoners were taken out from the school and put on buses; correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: As the prisoners were being taken out of the school and put on the buses, some of them were beaten and abused; right?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no. People were hurried to get onto the bus more quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: RS police members were beating and abusing these Muslim prisoners as they were getting on the buses; correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you -- perhaps someone was pushed to hurry them to get onto the bus, but there was civilian police and the army there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: One of the police officers that was doing this was Sreten Micic; right?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And Sreten Micic was participating in beating the prisoners as they were being put on the buses; right?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He was pushing people onto the bus to hurry them up.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Could we get 65 ter document 32111, page 20, on the monitor. And this is the investigative report that I've referred to several times during the cross-examination. Now, if we go to the second-last paragraph, and again the B/C/S should be at the same position as the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: It states: "Blagojevic was asked if he saw any of the prisoners in the buses or in the school being beaten or abused and he replied, 'yes,' that at the entrance to the school, as the prisoners were being taken out of the school and placed on the buses, he observed that the civilian police were beating and abusing the prisoners. He identified one of the police officers doing this as Sreten Micic." Mr. Blagojevic, that's correct, isn't it, that prisoners were being beaten and abused as they were taken from the school and put on the buses?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you again: People were pushed onto the bus because, as they were coming out of the school, they were hurried to get onto the bus as quickly as possible. There was shouting and there was pushing to get them onto the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, some Muslim prisoners were killed outside the Vuk Karadzic school in Bratunac on 14 July; correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That happened -- I mean, the shooting was behind the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: You saw some of the prisoners being killed, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Could we get 65 ter document 32112. This is the transcript of the videoed interview that we looked at yesterday as well. And if we could go to page 82 of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Now, if we look at the third intervention from the bottom, the question is asked: "Okay. You say the next morning that there were ... that some prisoners were killed outside the school. Explain to me what happened with that?"

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: If we skip across to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: "A. They were killed behind the school towards the hangar." "Q. What happened? "A. I don't know. "Q. How do you know they were killed? Did you see it or ...? "A. I saw some people being taken off the bus and being killed. "Q. Who were they taken off the bus by? "A. I don't know the people. I don't know these people." So, sir, in fact, you did see Muslim prisoners being taken off the bus and killed at the Vuk Karadzic school; correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you again, I saw they took them out of the bus and behind the school. Since I was in front of the school, and behind the school there is also a hangar, it was behind the school where I couldn't see it and that's what I said in my statement. I heard shots but I didn't see the killing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, could we clarify to which statement did you refer now, your statement given in the United States or your statement given to the Mladic Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's the statement about which the gentleman is questioning me. I told you I didn't see the killing. I saw them being taken behind the school.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please. The statement as recorded says: "I saw some people being taken off the bus and being killed," which, as far as my knowledge of the English language, is that you saw them being killed. So therefore, if you say, I say again, again, and again, you said something different at the time, and I think Mr. Gillett is trying to understand why you said that you saw them being killed at the time and why you now say that you only saw them disappearing behind the school. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. On the previous page it is explained, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, no. There is nothing. This is what the witness says after. He may have initially said something else. But this is what he says and I read it literally. And, Mr. Lukic, it's inappropriate to tell us that what the witness said before explains how we have to understand this. That is argument. I put some questions to the witness. That's our problem -- or Mr. Gillett's problem at this moment, Mr. Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am telling you I didn't see the killing, but I saw a couple of Muslims taken out of the bus and taken behind, but I didn't see it physically.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then the next question is: Do you have any explanation why you told at the time that you saw them being killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps I did not understand the question right, but I simply said that I saw them taken out, but I could not see through the school. It was behind the school.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can this page be scrolled up a little bit so that we can see the B/C/S answer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gillett, in view of the testimony of the witness this would be good -- this is not a CLSS translation. It is a transcript of an interview in which others have interpreted the words used by the witness. Perhaps it would be good and wise to have it verified whether this is an accurate interpretation of what was said.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: We will have that verified. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, the people that were taking the prisoners behind the school and killing them, were they wearing uniforms?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: What type of uniforms?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now I can't remember what kind of uniforms, but I believe they were in uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Were they military uniforms?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether they were military uniforms or police uniforms, blue ones. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: So to clarify they were either police uniforms or military uniforms; correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Now, you and the military police present still had the Browning gun at this stage outside the school; right?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: So you were armed and guarding the Muslim prisoners, but you didn't attempt to stop these people taking them from the buses and killing them, did you?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: "Yes" as in you agree that you did not attempt to stop these people; correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't dare.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: On that same day, you accompanied a column of buses with the Muslims prisoners from Bratunac up to Rocevic; correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And Mile Janjic was in the same vehicle as you accompanied them; right?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: At Rocevic, the Muslim prisoners were handed over to personnel from the Zvornik military brigade; right?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether it was the military police or somebody from the Zvornik Brigade, I don't know, because I was at the back of the column. Now who did the handing over? I was at the back of the column.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Can we get 65 ter document 32111, again, the investigative report. And if we go to page 4 of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And if we look at the second-last sentence or it may be the fourth-last sentence, starting: "Later that morning ..." It states: "Later that morning, Blagojevic and the other eight military policemen were ordered to provide security and follow the column of buses that departed Bratunac. The column travelled through Kravica and then to Rocevic where the prisoners were transferred into the custody of the Zvornik military personnel. The prisoners were unloaded at a school and held in the school's gymnasium. Blagojevic and the other eight military police officers returned to Bratunac, and the next morning they were assigned routine military police duties such as guard duty on the bridge and check-points." It's correct that the prisoners were handed to Zvornik military personnel in Rocevic; right?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: So when you just said that you weren't sure about that a few moments ago, that was not the truth, was it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You asked me whether -- whether we had handed them over to the military police of the Zvornik Brigade, and I told you that I was at the back of the column. Now, who was at the head of the column and who did the hand-over, I couldn't see that. Now, who did the talking around that hand-over, I don't know. But we handed them over to the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Sir, who ordered you to hand over the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. My group was only told to escort them, to go behind the convoy to prevent any attack along the way. Now, who ordered it, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Who ordered you to escort the column?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this point I'd tender 32111, which is the set of investigative reports we've been referring to during the testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 32111 receives number P7186.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is the report, not the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Not the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that report is how many pages?

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: That is 21 pages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7186 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. And on the transcript of the video, I'm suggesting, because it didn't always come through entirely clearly as to when it was a question and when it was an answer when I was reading from the transcript or when it was being played, that what I could do is take the existing transcript and take out the portions that have been read or played to the witness in court and have those made available. Obviously, if the Defence is agreeable to that suggestion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, a selection of the videoed interviews with the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I was informed by my colleague Stojanovic, as he was more familiar with that, that we would rather have the whole thing, not the selections, but because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But I think the usual practice is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I know that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- if a selection is made by the Prosecution, that the Defence may add any portions it considers relevant for context. Again, Mr. Lukic, if there are specific matters which are not contextual to the portions selected by the Prosecution, then, of course, you would have to put them to the witness, and you can't just introduce them otherwise.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: If --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: -- it may speed things up, we wouldn't object to the whole video coming in. We're also happy to take out the excerpts that have been played.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I suggest that the Prosecution and Defence will sit together, that the Prosecution explains to the Defence what selection it had on its mind, and that you will add whatever you think is needed even if that would be the complete video.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will proceed like that, and we already reserve a number for either excerpts or the entirety of the videoed interview of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the number reserved would be P7187.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that number stands.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: One final topic, Mr. Blagojevic. Yesterday during your testimony, you were asked by the Defence at transcript pages 32605 to 32606 the following: "Q. When you were entering the United States and receiving an immigration visa, did they ask you about your participation in the war? "A. Before we left for the United States, we went to Belgrade and we had a meeting with IOM. That was the name of the organisation. We had to fill in an application form. But they tricked us, in fact, and they told us not to report any participation in the war for purposes of speeding up our immigration." So you say that this IOM organisation tricked you into not reporting your membership in the VRS; right?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Previously, you've said that you left out the information about your involvement in the VRS from the immigration forms because you heard from family members that that was a way of getting into the US; correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That organisation told us not to report participation in the war in order to leave faster and to have families reunified.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: That wasn't my question. My question was whether you have previously said that you left off the information because family members told you that this was a way of speeding up the application process?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now you're putting something different to the witness as you did before. Earlier you said that the witness would have stated that he heard from family members that it was "a way of getting into the US," not on speeding up the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I'll repeat the full initial question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Sir, my question initially was: Previously, you've said that you left out the information about your involvement in the VRS from the immigration forms because you heard from family members that that was a way of getting into US; correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't hear that from family members. That is what we were told in the organisation of IOM in Belgrade, in order to get out faster.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Could we play the video 65 ter number 32155, and this clip is 00:38:00 to 00:40:35. Before we start playing, I would just note again that it has all the English and the B/C/S, so I suggest it's easier if we don't have interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's -- our interpreters will be surprised to hear that it's easier to have no interpretation, but under the circumstances I would agree that it's better to play the original without further explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: "We've been over it a couple of times, I've showed it to you. When you filled that out and you listed your military services as 1990 to 1992, why did you list it that way? "My wife was the carrier of that -- was the person that received the guarantee letter. I filled it out that way just to come here. "And you're -- so why did you leave the military service -- the Bratunac military service off of that form? "I was afraid that I won't be allowed to come here if I mention that. "Did anybody tell you that? Did anybody explain that to you? "The others who came earlier, they told me that. "The others -- other family members, other ...? "People who came here before. "Such as? "My wife's parents. My wife's brother. "Okay. Do you know if they were specifically instructed in Belgrade not to put that information in there? "I don't know. I'm not sure. "It was just -- it was just common knowledge or through family? "That was more in the family. It goes from one person to another. "So when you completed your application in Belgrade, a government worker or somebody didn't tell you to leave it off or anything? "No. "Okay. [Indiscernible] he's your brother-in-law" --

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: We can stop the video there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You started playing at 38:00. And we now stop looking at it at 40:31.8.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Sir, so, in fact, you did hear from family members that you should not put in the information about your VRS involvement on the immigration forms; correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's possible that I heard. But I repeat once again, perhaps I didn't remember to say this here, but I am telling you that the organisation IOM told us not to report participation in the last war. And it wasn't only my family and I that went there, hundreds and hundreds of other families went there too and did the same thing that I did. So it's this organisation that said this and I stand by that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I seek further clarification there. Did they tell you personally that this is the way you should do it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, personally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your testimony now is squarely contradicting what we hear in the videoed interview. Do you have any explanation why where quite a number of questions were put especially on this issue, that you give testimony today which is quite different from the answers you gave when interviewed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm telling you, possibly I didn't remember then. But later on, after having gone through everything and after having talked to people who, just like I, had a problem, I mean, they said that and that took me back to my memories of Belgrade and the IOM. Now I'm telling you that the organisation that was in Belgrade that is called IOM, they told us not to report participation in the last war. During those years in America, my eight years in America, I went there twice. It's not that I was hiding anything. But I'm telling you that I omitted to say that in that application. However, in that application, I cannot remember exactly, but I think it was something like did I take part in a foreign army. I did not consider the Army of Republika Srpska to be a foreign army. So the people who helped us with that application to go to America told us not to report participation in the last war in order to leave faster and to have family reunification. I state that with full responsibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gillett.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: I've no further questions, but I would add this excerpt from 65 ter 32155, which I'd also suggest I could discuss with the Defence adding that to the video package.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And, of course, we could play it again and then have it on the transcript. I think the best way of dealing with this is that the accompanying transcript pages to the video, that they should be tendered as well so that we have clearly what we just heard, that we have that as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: And Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see that it's fully in the transcript. I usually am constantly reading the transcript. I did not in this case because -- but we have the English text of the interview, we have that on the transcript already. Nevertheless, I think it would be good also in order to have a possibility to verify the accuracy of the language -- of the interpretation used and have it all on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: We'll do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In the exhibit, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: These were your questions. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I just have several questions, Your Honour. Thank you. Only for the record, it was proposed yesterday to this witness that there was a Prosecution witness who claimed that it was in front of General Mladic at that time when he was in Konjevic Polje, that one of the detained persons was killed. We would direct your attention, Your Honours, to the testimony of Prosecution Witness RM253 on the 12th of June, 2013, page 1254, where --

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd just note that that is a different witness to the one which I referred to in my question yesterday. Just to avoid any ambiguity.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, if you want to put to the witness another piece of evidence given by a witness, if that's relevant for questioning, you can do so and that -- just as Mr. Gillett could tell the witness what another witness said, you can do the same in the same context. But it's appreciated that you already have drawn our attention to the relevant transcript page so that we can follow it, if you have any questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I just wanted to put this on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Since we did not have any reference of what my learned friend -- actually, we did not get any reference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think it would have been in the -- Mr. Gillett, if you would have said another witness, Your Honours, transcript page so-and-so gives the reference, that would have been preferable, so that we can verify whether -- what exactly the source was you were quoting from. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Blagojevic, good day.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You heard yesterday that I would be standing in for my colleague, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you talked to the investigators in the United States of America, did you ever tell them in all of those interviews that you stopped in Konjevic Polje? Do you remember now?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember. But I know that we didn't stop in Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: To clarify the transcript, Mr. Lukic, I heard your question in the following way: "Did you ever tell them in all of those interviews ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And not "you."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, not "me." "Tell them."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It's clarified.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Today we looked at a document, and I'd like to go back to that, 65 ter 32112.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need the same page, 82, the one that my colleague had called up.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The very bottom of the page, it's in B/C/S as well, the translation of the question, you say: "The next morning, the next day, some prisoners were killed in front of the school. Can you explain that to me?" Your answer was: "Behind the school. Behind the school, over there, towards the hangar." And now let us move on to the next page. The middle of the page in B/C/S. "How do you know that they were killed? Did you see ..." Your answer: "I saw some people being taken off the bus and that someone was killing them. Now ..." And then you were interrupted there. In this section, did you want to change the place where the people had been killed, as you said on the previous page?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I said that they were taken behind the school towards the hangar. So since I was in front of the school and I could not see towards the hangar behind the school, there is nothing for me to change. I said that, that they took them behind the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Blagojevic. That is all I had for you.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic, I have one follow-up question in this respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If someone asks you how do you know they were killed, did you see it, in view of your testimony of today I would have expected an answer: No, I didn't see it because I couldn't see it because I was in front of the school and they were in the back of the school, rather than that you say that you saw them being taken away and being killed. Any explanation for that?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what I saw --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no, no --

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- well, a few soldiers --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What I'm interested in is how do you explain the difference between what you told in the US at the time and what you're telling us now?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm telling you that I personally, physically, did not see the killings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, your testimony of today is clear to us. What we are and what the parties may be struggling with is why you told otherwise when you were interviewed at the time?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I spoke in America, I said that they were taken behind the school.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you also said, did you see it, you confirmed that you saw them being taken away and saw them being killed. And, Mr. Lukic -- so therefore, you're telling us half of what you said in the US, and I draw your attention to the fact that you also confirmed that you saw it.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not confirm over there either that I had seen it. I am just repeating yet again --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please stop. There is no need to do that. Your testimony of today is clear. Mr. Lukic, I noted when you were putting this portion of the interview to the witness that the translation, the interpretation was slightly different from what we see on paper. And I found that there is a difference -- one second, please, so that I can take myself back to what you quoted. Yes. The difference is that in the English version of the interview, the language is: "I saw them being taken ... and being killed," whereas in the interpretation that we heard when you read this portion that: "I saw some people being taken off the bus and that someone was killing them," which is an even more direct link to observing the killing, because it says "someone." Now, I would very much like that portion to be verified, whether the translation as given at that time is the correct one, that is, the answer given by the witness, whether it's accurately interpreted by saying "I saw them being killed," or whether the accurate translation would be "someone was killing them." We don't need the witness to further verify this, but I'd like this to be dealt with in detail, and perhaps the parties could agree on what is the accurate translation and, perhaps with the assistance of CLSS, resolve the matter. Mr. Gillett.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Just one question for further re-examination arising from the -- sorry, for further cross-examination arising from the re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Sir, at temporary transcript line 20, line 5, you were asked: "When you talked to the investigators in the United States of America, did you ever tell me in all those interviews that you stopped in Konjevic Polje?" "A. Well, I don't remember, but I know that we didn't stop in Konjevic Polje." When I look at your transcript -- or, sorry, the statement that you gave to the Defence here in these proceedings, which is D922, at paragraph 9, you state: "After the general addressed the captured Muslims from Sandici, we headed down the road to Konjevic Polje where we briefly stopped at the police check-point where there were several civilian policemen on duty." So your answer in re-examination was different from the statement you've made at paragraph 9; correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BLAGOJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm saying that when we were going back from Sandici, General Mladic just stopped briefly. Now, was it through the window or through the open door, he just scolded these civilian policemen, that they were practically doing nothing. We almost didn't stop in Konjevic Polje. It was sort of in passing.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you Mr. Gillett. Witness, this concludes your testimony. We would like to thank you for coming the long way to The Hague and for having answered the questions that were put to you. I wish you a safe return home again and you may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GILLETT
utterances.text: Your Honours, just while the witness is being taken out, I'd just note for the record that yesterday when I was referring to the Prosecution witness who said that Mladic was present when a Bosnian Muslim was killed at Novo Kasaba, I gave the reference to the relevant transcript page, and you can see this at yesterday's transcript at 32620. Just for the record. I would also ask if myself and Mr. McCloskey could be excused prior to the next witness's testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please. Mr. Lukic, when you said no reference was given, first of all my recollection didn't serve me well. I take it that if you blame Mr. Gillett, as you did, for not having given a reference, that you would have verified that. You apparently didn't because he gave the reference. It's clearly on the record. Would you please next time verify before you make any such claims.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sorry, I apologise if I made a wrong accusation. And I cannot even check it now because our transcript is not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I did it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- updated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I did it for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I can tell you that it is accurate. Mr. Gillett is new, so I don't know whether he easily accepts apologies, yes or no. I know that there are quite some apologies to be accepted in this courtroom from my position from right to left and sometimes from left to right as well. We take a break and we will resume at ten minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are waiting for the next witness to enter the courtroom. It will be you, Mr. Ivetic, who will examine the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours. The next witness is Mr. Branko Volas, pursuant to 92 ter, no protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that. I could briefly deal with one matter which deals with P6698. On the 31st of October of last year, the Prosecution e-mailed the Chamber advising that it was prepared to make a brief in-court submission on the investigation into discrepancies in Exhibit P6698. The Chamber sets a dead-line for the Prosecution to make the submission in writing. The Chamber also notes the order of the original B/C/S pages of Exhibit P6698 and requests the Prosecution to submit a correct version. The matter was dealt with transcript pages 24794, 24804, and 24829 to 24831. I said I set a dead-line but I still have to tell you what that dead-line is. That would be next week, Tuesday, close of business. Could I ask the parties to try to be as efficient as possible so that the witness can leave The Hague before the weekend. The total time estimated is one hour and 30 minutes for cross, and 30 minutes for the Defence; therefore, two hours that should well fit into today's court session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Volas. Could you please stand for a second. Good morning, Mr. Volas. Before you give evidence, the Rules require that you make a solemn declaration. The text is now handed out to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Volas, you will first be examined by Mr. Ivetic. You will find Mr. Ivetic to your left. Mr. Ivetic is a member of the Defence team of Mr. Mladic. Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good day, sir. Could you please state your full name so that it correctly appears in the record.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO VOLAS
utterances.text: I am Branko Volas, born in 1954, in Kljuc. Father Luka, mother Rosa. I live in Zabrdje. I am father of two, retired.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can call up 65 ter number 1D1624 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us whose signature appears on the first page of this witness statement?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO VOLAS
utterances.text: It's my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can turn to the last page of the document in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, sir, on this page there is a signature above a date. Can you tell us whose signature we see here?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO VOLAS
utterances.text: It's my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, sir, subsequent to signing this statement on the date indicated, did you have a chance to read it over fully in the Serbian language to make sure that everything is correctly recorded in the statement?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO VOLAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And is everything accurately recorded in this statement?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO VOLAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I were to ask you questions today based upon the same topics as those in your written statement, would your answers today in substance be the same as the information which is contained in the written statement?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO VOLAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, sir, since you have taken a solemn declaration to tell the truth, does that mean that the answers as recorded in your statement are truthful in nature?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO VOLAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Defence would tender 1D1624 into evidence. There are no associated exhibits with that statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 1D1624 receives number D923.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D923 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have a short summary which has been explained to the witness. The witness Branko Volas testifies that before the conflict broke out in Kljuc, besides the police forces, mixed Serb and Muslim armed forces set up by the Territorial Defence were present in town. The first incidents in Kljuc were caused by Muslim extremists who attacked buses transporting unarmed JNA soldiers demobilised from the Croatian front, and ambushed and killed the deputy commander of the Kljuc police station. In certain villages inhabited by Muslims, check-points were set up which controlled the movement of Serbs. After these incidents, chaos ensued which lasted until the political authorities were in place. After the civilian authorities were established, they ordered that all citizens of Kljuc be protected. Everyone who did not possess illegal weapons nor pose a threat to Republika Srpska could remain in Kljuc. All those that had someone in third countries tried to leave Kljuc and go to a place where there was no war. This was done by Muslims, Croats, and Serbs alike. The corridor was closed and the connection with Serbia was cut off, so there was less food and medicine available. These conditions were difficult for all citizens of Kljuc. It was understandable that people would want to leave. And that ends the public summary.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, before we turn to some matters from your statement, sir, can you please tell us what position you held during the war and in what formation?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO VOLAS
utterances.text: Yes. I was mobilised in February 1992. It was still the JNA, the 13th Krajina Brigade, and its headquarters were in Banja Luka. I was an operations officer in the brigade command. And when unrests broke out in Kupres plateau, our unit was deployed at the demarcation line between the Croat, Muslim, and Serb territory. And I stayed there until 24 June 1992, when I was transferred to the Kljuc 17th Brigade to be assistant commander for intelligence and security in the battalion that was being set up then. Until 16 July, in Donja Previja, members for that unit were recruited and prepared for deployment. Around the 17th of August, we were transferred to the area of Grmec, towards Bihac, Grmusa sector, where we stayed for about 20 days on the demarcation line, and at that time I was appointed commander of the 3rd Battalion. In the beginning of August, we were sent on home leave, and after that we went about our duties pursuant to the orders from the command, and our tasks included mainly holding the separation line between the warring parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now I want to turn to page 2 of your statement, and I want to look at the second paragraph of the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So if we can call that up.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And here you talk of mixed Serb and Muslim armed forces that had been created by the Territorial Defence. First I want to ask you what about the active and reserve police forces which you mention, what was their composition?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO VOLAS
utterances.text: At that time before the end of May, there were both Serbs and Muslims in the reserve force of the police, and probably also the Territorial Defence. Since I was in one of these units, I noticed when I came back on leave from the Kupres plateau that in my street outside my building - and you have to know that Kljuc is a small town - I noticed that there were both Muslims and Serbs together in patrols. Patrols existed at that time to secure buildings, various installations, businesses, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, in relation to these mixed Serb and Muslim forces patrolling the town, what happened to them when the conflict broke out in Kljuc municipality?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO VOLAS
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you that because at that critical moment, I just arrived on leave from Kupres, and what happened later I don't know. While I was away, I couldn't see whether they continued to be mixed units and mixed patrols.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now if we could focus on the third paragraph in your statement on this same page. Can you provide us a time-frame for when these incidents, the attack on the bus of JNA soldiers and the ambush and killing of the deputy commander of the police station, a time-frame for when these incidents occurred?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which paragraph are we --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I know that was on 27 May. At that time, I was about 20 kilometres away from the scene, and I noticed that in the meantime reserve policemen had been called in. I knew some of them and they told me about this incident, that fire was opened at a convoy of military vehicles and Mr. Stojakovic, a deputy commander of the military police, was killed. After that I went home to see my wife and children and see what the situation was like. I saw that something was going on. I saw that there was anxiety on both sides, and there were ambulances and other emergency vehicles moving around more than usual. So it all began during those days.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now in this same paragraph, you identify: "In certain villages and settlements that were predominantly inhabited by Muslims, they set up check-points and controlled the movement of Serbs." Can you specify for us what village or villages are at issue here?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO VOLAS
utterances.text: On that day, my wife's brother was visiting his father in Pec village, which is between Sanski Most and Kljuc. And when he was passing by bus through Krasulje, going to Sanski Most, the vehicle was stopped. He knew those people. He saw that they were armed Muslims. They didn't create any problems, they let the people go on. But in the same place, Stojakovic was later killed. I know that from reliable sources. I don't know anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- if a witness says that he knows something on the basis of reliable sources, then of course the reliability is for the Chamber to decide. Could you further explore those sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, you've heard what the Judges have said. Could you provide more details as to the sources of this information that you have just referenced?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO VOLAS
utterances.text: That information came from my wife's brother, who saw me that very day. He told me that and I believe him, and that's the only reliable information that I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Witness, you told us that your brother-in-law came across those check-points. Did you have any personal experience at check-points?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Between my village, Zabrdje, and Kljuc, there is a settlement --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- where I passed through after all these incidents. I didn't see, I didn't notice anyone armed or standing unarmed on the road, nor were there any problems on the way through that area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the only source of knowledge is your brother-in-law. Now, you also said that someone was killed at that same check-point at a later point in time, Mr. Stojakovic. What is your source of knowledge of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know that area. I passed through that place many times, Krasulje village, where Stojakovic was killed. You have a very good view of that area. You can see both vehicles and people. It was a road under their control. It was safe for them and they probably shot him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: They probably shot him. So it is -- you think that he would have been shot there, but you are not certain about it. Is that how I have to understand your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, after the bus arrived in Kljuc, the police was informed that there was this incident with a bus and passengers, and the police came out to investigate, and that's how it happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but what is now your specific source of knowledge about Mr. Stojakovic being killed, by whom? Who told you or did you see it or ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. At that time I wasn't there. I was 20 kilometres away, as I said. The people who were with him told me that, members of the police who were with him in the car. And I believe there was more than one car. They were all met with gun-fire but they managed to pull back and escape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can turn to page 4 in both languages of your statement, I'd like to ask you a question about paragraph 13 of the same. Sir, in paragraph 13 you say: "The Serbs were armed legally through the army." Could you please explain for us what you meant to say here? What kind of Serb persons were so armed?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO VOLAS
utterances.text: I can maintain that only about those Serbs who were mobilised into JNA units at the time, and of course when they were mobilised they were given weapons. Whether there was illegal arming or not, I don't know that since I was already part of a unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I ask a question?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sir, the JNA was a mixed army, wasn't it? I mean, there were Croats and Muslims and Serbs in it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And all of the members of the army would have been legally armed by the JNA, isn't it so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That would include the Muslims and the Croats?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, those who actually responded to the call-up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So the JNA had always had people -- we're not talking about something that is created during the war, but we're talking about the JNA that was existing before the war.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before the war, the units did not arm men when they were at home. They were given weapons only when they assembled at a given place, when they were mobilised, so we did not have any weapons at home. You got a weapon only when you were mobilised and when a unit was formed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And who armed these Serbs at this point in time legally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At that time the units that were in charge; that's to say, levels above brigade. In pre-war conditions, there were commands for the development of so-called partisan units that were in charge of such tasks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But my question is: What authority was arming these Serb people who were legally armed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not authorities. It's the official JNA that was in JNA barracks, and in those barracks, weapons and equipment were held. And on the orders of a superior command, these development commands would bring weapons to the assembly place. And when men were mobilised, they would come to that assembly point, receive weapons, and at that time it wouldn't matter whether they were Muslim, Croat, or Serb.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But you say in that the Serbs legally armed and they were armed by the JNA, so I would expect that the JNA didn't arm them, the Croats and the Muslims. From what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are not understanding each other. I said in February 1992 there was still JNA, and within those partisan units of the JNA - for instance, in our specific unit - there were both Muslims and Croats. And, of course, they received weapons at the time as well. However, later on they kept the weapons and left the units. Some stayed within the units, but a lot of people left and kept their weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, on behalf of General Mladic and the rest of the team, I thank you for answering my questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, that completes my direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ivetic. Before I give an opportunity to the Prosecution to cross-examine the witness, I have one question for you in relation to paragraph 14. And it's a very short paragraph, so I'll read it to you in its entirety: "At the time of the incidents cited in the indictment, I was in the war theatre at Kupres. I do not know anything about the number of victims and the incident itself." It is not entirely clear what incident you are talking about. You are talking about incidents cited in the indictment, but there are many. Could you tell us which one you had on your mind when you said that you did not have any knowledge about the number of victims and the incident itself? What incident were you talking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've already said when you asked me where I was and what I did during all these things that happened. I said that on the 24th of June I was at Kupres; that is to say, that is more than 100 kilometres away from the place where this was happening. And then I was in Donja Previja at the mobilisation of the 3rd Battalion --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We don't hear the witness anymore.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me stop you there, because you may have misunderstood my question. You said, "I was 100 kilometres away," but what is the incident you are talking about? What is it? Was it an expulsion of persons, was it a killing, was it wounding, was it people being fired from their jobs? I've got no idea what incident you are talking about in paragraph 14, and I'm asking you to tell me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, probably when this statement was being taken, a question was put about incidents in the area of Velagici. Now, what was the name of that village? Prhovo and so on. Probably that was the question put to me. That's why I said that I had no knowledge. I don't know of the number of victims. I don't know where it happened exactly, and who did all of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you don't remember exactly which incident you are telling us you have no knowledge of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We cannot understand what the witness is saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the microphone be adjusted for the witness. Perhaps you -- my question was whether you don't remember exactly which incident you are telling us about of which you have no knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have no knowledge about -- you don't know that. Did you look in the indictment at the time? Because you are talking about incidents in the indictment. Were you familiar with the indictment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. The persons who spoke to me when I was giving the statement assumed that there would be questions about these incidents because the indictment has to do with what happened in the area of Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did they tell you exactly about these incidents? Did they explain to you what they were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you're telling us that you don't know about something which you don't even know what it is that you don't know about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, everything I knew came from much later. People talked. You know, it's a small community and people talk about things, and things that people talk about I cannot say are true or not true. You know what it's like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But in many respects, you told us that you learned just from others what had happened. So you don't know whether that's true or not what you learned about Mr. Stojakovic being killed when you were 20 kilometres away?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, I heard about that. The man was killed and I attended the funeral.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I leave it to that. Mr. Jeremy, if you're ready to cross-examine the witness, you may start doing so.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. And good morning. And just at the outset, full disclosure: I initially estimated an hour and a half for this witness and I revised it down subsequently to an hour, which in an hour's time might be something I regret, but I'm going to aim to stick to that hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are encouraged to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, sir, I'd like to return to paragraph 14 of your statement, which we've just been discussing. Now, charged in the indictment is an incident relating to Kljuc on or about the 1st of June, 1992, and that's the -- that incident is the killing of at least 77 men at Velagici school. Now, I understand from your testimony today that you were in Kupres at this time; correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO VOLAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, the -- another incident charged in the indictment relating to Kljuc is on the 10th of July, 1992, and that relates to the killing of at least 144 people in Biljani. Now, I understand from your testimony today that you returned from Kupres on the 24th of June, 1992, when you were transferred to the 17th Brigade as assistant commander for intel and security. So were you, in fact, in Kljuc on the date of this particular incident, the 10th of July, 1992?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO VOLAS
utterances.text: No, I was assistant commander of a battalion, and it was being established in Donja Previja. That is 12 or 13 kilometres away from Kljuc in the area of --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters did not hear the rest.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Sir, could you repeat the final part of your answer? You said that you were assistant commander of the battalion and -- which was established in Donja Previja. "That's 12 or 13 kilometres away from Kljuc in the area of ..." and we didn't hear the area. If you could repeat that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could all other microphones please be switched off when the witness is speaking.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the area of Ribnik and Banja Luka, in that direction. On one side is Biljani. On the other side -- I mean, Kljuc, so then Donja Previja is out there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could you also speak slightly louder.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, sir, in relation to these incidents occurring in Kljuc in a general sense, you said that people were talking about them. Now, as part of this talk, did you hear that Marko Samardzija, a company commander in the 2nd Battalion of the 17th Brigade, was involved in this particular incident in Biljani?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO VOLAS
utterances.text: No. No. I knew Marko before the war. After that I didn't see him. I didn't have any contact with him. Especially because, at that time, part of the unit was at the Bihac theatre of war, another one at the Jajce theatre of war. There was no contact between the units. I did not know who was there and what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: So, to be clear, you had no contact with Marko Samardzija during the war period, is that correct, between 1992 and 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We cannot hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know where he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Sir, could you repeat your answer, please?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO VOLAS
utterances.text: I had no contact with Samardzija, and I did not see him during the war, and I don't know where he was. I never noticed him in the 2nd Battalion, and I did have contact with the 2nd Battalion at the end of June at --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters did not hear the name of the plateau.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is to say, 100 kilometres away from Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, again, could you speak up a bit louder and come a bit closer to the microphones. The interpreters have repeatedly difficulties in hearing you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And, sir, you mentioned a particular plateau, and the interpreters did not capture the name of that plateau. Could you repeat it, please.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO VOLAS
utterances.text: Grmusa plateau. That's the territory of the municipality of Bihac. Between Bosanska Krupa and Bihac there is Grmec.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, today you were you were appointed commander of the 3rd Battalion around August or September 1992. Now, you were replaced as the commander of the 3rd Battalion at the end of October 1994; correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO VOLAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And you were replaced by Bozo Davidovic; correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO VOLAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And you were replaced as commander of the 3rd Battalion because there were concerns that you were making arrangements to leave your battalion's position at the time; correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO VOLAS
utterances.text: I don't think that that is what is charged in the indictment. I think it was something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Sir, you refer to an indictment. Could you explain what indictment you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO VOLAS
utterances.text: Probably this one on account of which I'm testifying here today.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Sir, when you said that you think something else was charged in the indictment, can you explain what you meant?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO VOLAS
utterances.text: Could you please repeat that question? I did not quite understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Well, sir, I suggested to you that you were -- the reason you were replaced as commander of the 3rd Battalion was because there were concerns that you were making arrangements to leave your battalion's position in October 1994. Now in response you said to me: "I don't think that that is what is charged in the indictment. I think it was something else." So could you clarify what you're referring to as you think it was something else?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO VOLAS
utterances.text: Well, because there were no proceedings against me, disciplinary or court proceedings, in relation to what happened. I was simply reassigned to a different unit, to the same position.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's take a quick look at an exhibit in connection with this, which might be able to assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Could we please see P362, and that's the notebook of General Mladic. And could we go to page 115 in the English and 114 in the B/C/S, please. Sorry, could we go to the -- I should have said. Could we go to the typed B/C/S version of the diary? My mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, sir - thank you - on the screen before you, we see this is General Mladic's diary and we see an entry relating to the 13th of October, 1994, and we see that there is a meeting with commanders of the RSK. And we see a reference to the 1st and 2nd Krajina Corps and some additional corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Could we please go to page 121 in the English and 120 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, sir, directing your attention to the bottom of the page on the screen before you, we see a reference to a Mitrovic. That's a reference to Colonel Mikajlo Mitrovic, the chief of intel and security in the 2nd Krajina Corps; yes?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We did not understand the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you repeat your answer and speak up a little bit more, because if we can't hear you, we can't ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I knew Colonel Mitrovic personally. Now, what duty he had in the corps command, that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Okay. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Could we go to the next page in each language, please. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: So, sir, referring your attention to the second hyphenated paragraph, I read as follows: "- In the 3rd Battalion of the 17th Brigade - it has been proven that Captain 1st Class Branko Volas was making arrangements with star commanding officers and company commanders to leave the battalion position." Now, firstly, sir, that's a reference to yourself, correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO VOLAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now this entry appears to suggest that you were indeed making arrangements to leave the battalion position. Can you explain what this entry actually relates to?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO VOLAS
utterances.text: I think that that is the personal opinion of Colonel Mitrovic. At that time, I carried out the orders issued to me by my superior command of the brigade, and that meant moving the unit to reserve positions which made it possible to act better. This was done on orders from the brigade command.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: But it was because of this position that you were -- it was because of the decision that you took that you were removed from your position as battalion commander; correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO VOLAS
utterances.text: That was not my decision. That was implementation of orders from the superior command.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And what position did you take after you were removed as battalion commander?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO VOLAS
utterances.text: For a while after the situation became different in the 15th Bihac Brigade, I was company commander and then battalion commander. And that's where I was until the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jeremy, the Chamber wonders, not only in respect to the cross-examination but for the entirety, perhaps, of the testimony of the witness, what the relevance is. We do not see anything, in his statement at least, about his functions, et cetera, that was introduced today. Of course, the 65 ter summary tells us that he would tell us a lot of things about all kind of things where we do not find anything in his statement about most of it. And now, apparently, there has once been a problem in whether or not this witness was a reliable officer or not, I take it. We don't know exactly what happened but -- and now we are spending a lot of time on that. Could you either come to your point quickly or explain to us what the relevance of this is? And perhaps we should have asked the question for the whole of this testimony to the Defence as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I simply wanted to explore this entry[ relating to the witness departing from his position as battalion commander. It's not something that's mentioned in his statement. But if it's not of -- I see it's not of assistance to the Chamber, so I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I do not know. Apparently someone has had, and perhaps the accused may have had, at some time a concern about this witness perhaps leaving with his battalion. And then he says, Well, that was not the case and I've never been prosecuted for that. So we are dealing with a totally isolated incident which apparently has got nothing to do with the indictment, at least as far as we understand from the evidence as presented until now. And are we going to listen to those details for another hour?

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, the position of the Prosecution would be that this is a clear example of command and control being exercised by the accused. Concerns about this witness as a battalion commander are expressed in the diary entry of Mr. Mladic. Shortly after that, the witness is removed from his position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. I see your point. And I can also imagine that in view of what was announced in the 65 ter summary, that you would expect evidence of this kind, and it was introduced only today. Let's then briefly deal with that. You've now explained what the relevance is, and I think we could deal with that easily in ten, perhaps 15 minutes, isn't it? If it's just that issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. And I'm satisfied the issue has been sufficiently dealt with now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, if the Prosecution is going to stand up and give their position, I think it's only fair that the Defence stands up and gives their position on this evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the reason, first of all, I intervened during cross-examination and I addressed the cross-examiner. And I was about to give you an opportunity to make any submissions you think would be important at this moment. Perhaps one of them, if you could clarify, why there is such a huge difference between the 65 ter summary and what we find in the statement of the witness. That would certainly be appreciated. If you can do it in a few words.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With respect to the 65 ter summary, I don't know who prepared it for this witness. It was not myself. But I think that the information was not yet available to us fully as to what the witness would testify about. I believe the statement is dated after the date that the 65 ter would have been submitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, if you say the witness will testify about the composition of his battalion and its activities, well, whether the evidence is there depends on what you present. You -- there is no way that you could say, "Well, we didn't know yet what the witness would testify about," because he'll testify about what you ask him. He'll testify about what you put in his statement. Apparently, you have changed your mind in this respect. But please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And -- proceed to whom?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, to you, Mr. Ivetic --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- because you were -- I interrupted you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That is correct. Now, in relation to this that has just been shown to the witness, it would be the Defence's position that this demonstrates that there was oftentimes questions about the veracity of information that was coming up through the reporting. And that given the evidence of this witness that he's just now given, that has demonstrated that what was reported in this meeting is not in accord with what the witness presents or the factual scenario at the time. And that would be the position of the Defence. And I thank you for that and apologise for taking up this much time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Jeremy.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. And I will move on from this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Could we -- and we'll go back, sir, to Kljuc in 1992 and focus on paragraph 3 of your statement. Now in this paragraph 3, you refer to preparations that were being made for war by "Muslim extremists." The Serb leadership in Kljuc were also organising militarily in the months leading up to the conflict; correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO VOLAS
utterances.text: Since I was in a JNA unit at the time, what the Serb leadership in the municipality of Kljuc was doing then, I don't know. I don't know what you consider to be the Serbian leadership. Is that the Territorial Defence or is it politics?

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Well, sir, I'd like to show you an exhibit in connection with that and I think that will answer your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I know we're close to the break time. This area will probably take me five minutes or so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then how much time would you then need after the break?

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: I think I've probably taken around 20 minutes or so. I'll -- I will finish in the next session after the break, comfortably.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll take a break. But could you please consider to see -- a witness who has testified that he doesn't know anything about A and knows everything about B but gives hardly any sources of knowledge, and the sources of knowledge he testified about, well, may require reassessment of the importance and of the accuracy of the whole of the testimony. Could you please consider all that and see how much time you would need after the break after you've thought this over.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We take a break, Witness. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes. And we'll then continue. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at ten minutes past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're waiting for the witness to be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jeremy, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Now, sir, at the end of the last session we were discussing the Serb leadership in Kljuc. Now, that's something that I will come back to, but now I'd like to switch topics.
